## Background

There are many *graphic systems* in R for making plots and figures. These include **"base R graphics"** like the `plot()` and add-on packages like **ggplot2**.

Let's compare how we make a simple graph with these two systems

We can use the in-built `cars` dataset: 
```{r}
head(cars)
```


A base R plot:

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now for **ggplot2**.

Before I can use ggplot2 I need to install it on my computer. To do this we can use the function `install.packages("ggplot2")`

> **N.C.** We never run an `install.packages()` in our quarto doc (we run it in our R console) as it would re-install the package every time I render my document.

Once installed you still need to load up the package into our R session. We do this with a `library()` call
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```


Every ggplot needs at least 3 inputs:

- the **data** (a data.frame of the new stuff we want to plot)
- the **aesthetics** (how the data maps to the plot),
- the **geom** layer (how do you want the plot drawn, points, lines etc,)

```{r}
ggplot(cars)+ 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist)+
  geom_point()
```

## Lets add some features (more layers)

Let's add a trend line that shows the relationship between `speed` and `distance`:

```{r}
ggplot(cars)+ 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist)+
  geom_point()+ 
  geom_line()
```

```{r}
ggplot(cars)+ 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist)+
  geom_point()+ 
  geom_smooth()
```
Add a theme, custom axis labels and plot title:
```{r}
ggplot(cars)+ 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist)+
  geom_point()+ 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(x="Speed (mph",
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)",
       title= "Stopping distance of some old cars")
```



## Gene Expression Plot

First we will read some expression data for the effects of a GLP-1 drug

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes)+
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2,col=State)+
  geom_point() +
 scale_colour_manual( values=c("blue","gray","red"))+
theme_bw ()+
    labs(x="No drug",
         y="Drug",
     title="GLP-1 Inhibitor Effects on Gene Expression")
                        
```
```{r}
table(genes$State)
```

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```
```{r}
colnames(genes)
ncol(genes)
```

```{r}
n.total <- nrow(genes)
n.up <- sum(genes$State =="up")
         
         n.up/n.total
```
```{r}
sum(genes$State =="up")/nrow(genes)
```

## Going Further


```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
head(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many entries are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> how many different "country" values are in this dataset?

```{r}
length(table(gapminder$country))
```

```{r}
length( unique(gapminder$country))
```

notes functions:

- nrow()
- table ()
- unique ()
- length ()


Let's make our first plot of `gdpPercap` vs `lifeExp`:

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder, aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.2)
```



```{r}
ggplot(gapminder, aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp,col=continent)) +
  geom_point()
```


One useful layer we can add to explore big datasets like this is called "facetting"

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder, aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp, col = continent)) +

  geom_point() +

  facet_wrap(~continent)
```


### Limit to 1977 and 2007

We can install and use **dplyr** package to help us "filter" the full dataset down to a smaller subset that only includes the years we want.

First we need to run `install.packages("dplyr")` and then load it with `library(dplyr)`.


```{r}
library(dplyr)
filter(gapminder,year==2007, country=="Ireland")
filter(gapminder,year==1977, country=="Ireland")
#gapminder$year
```

> Q. Make a histogram of lifeEXP

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder)+
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent)+
  geom_histogram()
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder)+
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent)+
  geom_boxplot()
```




```{r}
library(dplyr)
filter(gapminder,year==2007, country=="United States")
#gapminder$year
```


```{r}
gapminder$year
```
